forces.title: Shift to 'always-on' travel inspiration via social media and AI
forces.description: Travel planning is no longer a linear path but a 'looping orbit,' with inspiration continuously delivered through social feeds, film, and AI. Sixty percent of travelers cite social media as a top-three inspiration source, and 70% have discovered new destinations this way. This necessitates continuous engagement and credible content from travel providers, as ideas casually discovered can be easily discarded without commitment, increasing competition for sustained traveler attention.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Fragmented research creates 'restart tax' and decision fatigue
forces.description: Travelers use nine or more channels for trip research, but these tools rarely share context, forcing travelers to repeat searches, re-enter preferences, and reconstruct decision maps across platforms. This 'restart tax' leads to the most frequent source of negative sentiment during research and can cause travelers to abandon one trip orbit for another, as new ideas are always available frictionlessly, while research often is not. Overwhelming choice causes anxiety.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Booking confirmation now a waypoint, not a final decision
forces.description: The traditional 'buy' button no longer signifies the end of the travel planning journey. Flexible change and cancellation policies, continuous price monitoring, and a constant stream of new recommendations mean booking decisions are less final. Half of travelers have changed booked accommodations after seeing a more attractive option, indicating an active post-booking relationship is crucial for operators and highlighting ongoing competition even after a reservation is made.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Trusted sources and social proof crucial for converting inspiration
forces.description: As inspiration becomes abundant, earning credibility is paramount. Friends and family are the most trusted source of recommendations for 65% of travelers, and 46% turn to them at the inspiration stage due to comparability. Travel creators and user-generated content are also highly influential (67% rank them among top three trusted sources), with authenticity and relatability driving confidence and conversion. Operators must integrate social proof and empower staff to create 'story-worthy' experiences.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI's speed in answering queries increases total research time
forces.description: Despite AI offering faster answers to individual queries, nearly 60% of respondents agree that it causes them to spend more total time researching. The speed allows travelers to ask more questions, open more tabs, and reconsider options, leading to deeper, but not necessarily faster, decision-making. This complexity adds to decision fatigue, as travelers are constantly presented with opportunities to refine or re-evaluate their choices, prolonging the research phase.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Growing global wellness economy creates tailwinds for leisure services
forces.description: The global wellness economy is projected to grow approximately 8% annually through 2030, outpacing many other discretionary categories. This expansion is driven by consumers broadening their definition of fitness to include overall wellbeing, such as mental health and longevity. This trend provides powerful tailwinds for leisure facilities like fitness centers and other wellness services, as consumers are increasingly willing to invest in holistic health-related experiences and products beyond traditional activewear.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: AI transforms product and service discovery in wellness and travel
forces.description: AI is becoming increasingly influential in consumer discovery, with 36% of US consumers using it for shopping and over 50% across wellness 'occasions.' Consumers are shifting from specific product searches to broader, holistic questions. This provides a new platform for wellness and travel service providers to be discovered, especially during high-intent life stages (e.g., beginning a weight-loss journey or training for a marathon) if offerings are optimized for AI-generated recommendations.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: Softening consumer demand impacts Irish restaurant and food services
forces.description: Irish food services are facing a challenging backdrop, with both sales value and volume declining. Demand continues to shift towards limited-service restaurants, indicating a more value-conscious consumer environment across hospitality. This trend suggests that consumers are tightening discretionary spending on dining out, potentially due to broader economic pressures and cost-of-living challenges, placing pressure on full-service restaurant operators.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Shortened booking lead times increase revenue management complexity
forces.description: Irish hotel operators are reporting shorter booking windows and a rise in last-minute bookings this year. This trend, likely driven by evolving consumer behavior or uncertainty, presents challenges for revenue management, making it harder to predict demand and optimize pricing effectively. Operators need to adapt their strategies to manage this volatility and protect profitability, potentially by leveraging technology for more agile pricing and inventory control.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Technology adoption critical for Irish hospitality operational efficiency
forces.description: Technology adoption, including AI, automation, revenue management tools, and energy monitoring, is becoming essential for Irish hospitality operators. These tools are crucial for protecting service standards and margins amidst persistent cost pressures and labor challenges. Investment in digital transformation is no longer optional but a necessary strategy to improve productivity, optimize labor scheduling, manage costs, and enhance the guest experience.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Domestic demand stabilizes Irish regional and shoulder-season hotel trading
forces.description: Irish residents continue to underpin regional and shoulder-season trading for the hospitality sector, especially where value and experience are clearly positioned. This domestic demand acts as a crucial stabilizer against external demand fluctuations, providing a resilient base for hotel operators. Maintaining relevance and tailored offerings for local customers is key for protecting revenues outside of peak international tourism periods.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: State-contracted accommodation returning to Irish tourism supply
forces.description: The phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation (for Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection/International Protection) is improving tourism availability. Registered bed stock under contract has fallen from 13.0% in summer 2023 to 3.7% in May 2026, with full withdrawal expected by March 2027. This gradual return of beds provides a measured supply-side tailwind, potentially improving destination capacity and supporting commercial tourism in certain regional markets, though impact will vary by location.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Food services impacted by value-conscious consumers and declining volumes
forces.description: Irish food services are experiencing a challenging environment with declining sales value and volume, as consumers become more value-conscious and shift towards limited-service restaurants. This indicates a general pullback in discretionary spending on dining out. Operators face pressure to balance rate growth with service consistency and product quality, as pricing power in this segment is being scrutinised more heavily by consumers.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical disruption negatively impacts high-value long-haul travel demand
forces.description: Geopolitical risk is a direct demand variable for Irish hospitality. Bank of Ireland card-spend data shows declines in airline spending and weaker spend from the US and Gulf States. This suggests that higher long-haul costs, security concerns, and geopolitical uncertainty are influencing travel decisions. While softer outbound air travel may support domestic staycations, sustained geopolitical deterioration could weigh heavily on inbound sentiment, corporate travel, and high-value North American demand for Irish hotels.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: US consumer net spending intent negative for hotels, restaurants, food delivery
forces.description: Consumer sentiment in the US indicates a persisting discretionary restraint, with net spending intent registering -22% for hotel and resort stays, -20% for food delivery services, and -18% for meals at sit-down restaurants. While these figures are specific to the US, they highlight a broad consumer trend of pulling back on non-essential services. If this sentiment transmits to Europe, it represents a significant headwind for the Consumer Services sector.
forces.source_title: An update on US consumer sentiment: Holiday budgeting begins

viewpoints.title: AI adoption in travel is advancing faster than operator readiness
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's survey indicates that 71% of travelers are comfortable using AI for trip inspiration today, and 86% would consider AI bookings in the future. Despite this high consumer comfort, operator readiness lags, with many still grappling with how to integrate AI effectively. AI adds speed to planning but trust remains a barrier, as travelers often verify AI-generated itineraries with human-backed sources. This creates both permission and pressure for travel players to adapt quickly.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Customer reviews and authentic content drive higher hotel conversion rates
viewpoints.description: Accor's chief commercial officer, Alix Boulnois, confirms that A/B tests on hotel pages reveal customer reviews significantly boost conversion. Transparency, even about imperfections, creates more confidence than curated brand narratives. Travelers prioritize genuine feedback and relatable guest experiences over polished campaigns when making booking decisions. This suggests that authentic user-generated content and transparent feedback are critical marketing assets for hotels.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Curated travel options preferred over extensive catalogs or single AI plans
viewpoints.description: Travelers express a clear preference for curated options, with 63% choosing a platform offering ten recommended options based on budget and preferences, compared to 30% for 500 options with filters and 7% for a single AI-generated plan. Consumers desire a credible short list, clear reasoning for choices, and the ability to compare or adjust, highlighting a need for guided discovery rather than overwhelming choice or absolute automation.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Hotels need clear positioning and differentiation to protect pricing power
viewpoints.description: The Irish hospitality market is polarising, with strong investor and customer momentum at luxury/lifestyle and budget/value ends. Mid-market and larger independent hotels are advised to establish clearer positioning, brand affiliation, or experience-led differentiation to maintain relevance and pricing power. New entrants in Northern Ireland are increasingly brand-led, boutique, or hybrid, highlighting the competitive pressure on undifferentiated offerings.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Dublin hotel market H2 2026 outlook cautiously positive, RevPAR growth rate-led
viewpoints.description: The H2 2026 outlook for Dublin's hotel market remains cautiously positive, forecasting stable occupancy at 83.8% and a modest 1.1% RevPAR growth over 2025. This growth is primarily driven by Average Daily Rate (ADR) increases rather than significant occupancy gains. Summer demand, air capacity, and events are expected to support trading. Operators need to focus on converting RevPAR growth into cashflow amidst cost inflation and shifting supply dynamics.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Hospitality H2 is about margin conversion, not just volume recovery
viewpoints.description: For H2 2026, Irish hospitality operators must prioritize converting RevPAR growth into cashflow rather than solely focusing on volume recovery. This requires disciplined cost control, strategic payroll deployment, effective procurement, and efficient channel mix management. While trading momentum is positive, persistent cost inflation, value-conscious consumers, and shifting supply dynamics necessitate a focus on operational efficiencies to protect margins.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish hospitality faces high insolvency risk due to fuel and transport costs
viewpoints.description: The Irish hospitality sector, including pubs and restaurants, is expected to continue experiencing a high proportion of insolvencies for the remainder of 2026. Profitability is tightening due to rising fuel prices and increased processing and transport costs, linked to the Middle East conflict. Smaller producers, processors, and hospitality-linked operators need careful cash-flow forecasting and supplier term review as insolvency pressure remains elevated.

demand_drivers.description: Consumers increasingly view fitness through the lens of overall wellbeing, including cardiovascular health, weight management, longevity, and mental wellbeing, rather than just exercise alone. This holistic view drives spending across a broader set of wellness categories.

Wellness spending accelerates during specific life moments such as youth sports participation, weight-loss journeys, and setting new fitness goals, which are 'accelerant moments' for acquiring new consumers and increasing wallet share for wellness services. Conversely, parenthood, injury, or healthy aging are 'retention moments' that shift spending toward adjacent wellness categories.

new_opportunities.description: Activewear brands can build relevance with younger consumers by partnering with fast-growing fitness communities, workout formats, and athletic events, such as workout classes, running clubs, and fitness competitions, which are a form of leisure facility.

Consumers are increasingly using AI to ask holistic questions about wellness needs (e.g., 'What gear do I need to train for my first marathon?'). Brands can establish authority by ensuring their services and advice are visible within AI-generated recommendations during these high-intent moments, enabling new discovery journeys for wellness services.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Leveraging AI for discovery of wellness services

market_sizing.methodology: The global wellness economy is projected to grow significantly, indicating a broader consumer shift towards health and wellbeing, which includes various services such as fitness and leisure.
market_sizing.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

demand_drivers.driver: Corporate demand, events, and air access
demand_drivers.description: Dublin continues to benefit from these factors, supporting a stable and slightly growing RevPAR despite increased capacity in recent years.
Seasonal peaks in inbound travel support trading performance.
The phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation is expected to gradually improve tourism accommodation availability, acting as a supply-side benefit.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecast for full year 2026 in Dublin, based on CoStar STR & Tourism Economics. ADR of €176.11 and occupancy of 83.8%. RevPAR is ADR * Occupancy.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026
